### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**4** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **14** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9bff554ef125649be4887880a2e3ac75f14de02b` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c3a1a543a00ee20e669fc93d9f0bef27c8398c2f` — the merge of head `9d2a0f127acec9d44caf17fee583064d6bba6880` into base `9bff554ef125649be4887880a2e3ac75f14de02b`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c3a1a543a00ee20e669fc93d9f0bef27c8398c2f && git checkout c3a1a543a00ee20e669fc93d9f0bef27c8398c2f
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 9bff554ef125649be4887880a2e3ac75f14de02b 9d2a0f127acec9d44caf17fee583064d6bba6880 && git checkout -B drift-repro 9bff554ef125649be4887880a2e3ac75f14de02b && git merge --no-ff 9d2a0f127acec9d44caf17fee583064d6bba6880

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 9bff554ef125649be4887880a2e3ac75f14de02b
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`

Not read: partial-index-probe.ts, the dogfood upgrade fixtures, ADR-0131 itself (its D1 is taken as the diff cites it).

Check-runs on this head (polled 2026-11-10T21:25Z): **"every check green" is not met** — 19 runs are unfinished. In progress: Build Core; Test Core 1/8 to 8/8; Type Check · workspace; Type Check · consumer gates; Type Check · debt ledger; Lint · ESLint; Lint · CI, release & engine gates; Lint · docs & code guards; Lint · repo & tooling gates; Lint · scoped · query-options erasure; Lint · scoped · slot lookup & corpus; Live E2E UI. Skipped by job condition, so no verdict here: Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL), 18.x upgrade harness (opt-in), the Dogfood shards, the UI build/type/lint jobs, Packed-tarball smoke. The PR is a draft, `mergeable_state: blocked`.

### ① Derived judgments

- **18.0 NULL-safe narrower: right.** `present` now admits, on the widening arm only (`l.widenedBy` set), an index with the narrower's columns whose single expression key part is the tenant column's COALESCE form (`isNullSafeTenantNarrower`: exactly one expression, exactly one null-safe column, and it is `tenantField`). The tenant arms keep the old plainness rule. Not certified: kept, nothing offered, never an orphan. Certified: kept until a partial guard on the narrower columns stands, then one `replace_unique_index`, `safe`, whose `actual` and message now show the COALESCE form. This is the ruling of 6774415127 ("one safe replace only on a certified table, never an orphan drop").
- **Gained column not yet physical: right.** The old `listed.every(physical)` bail is replaced by: skip only if every listed column is absent, never enumerate a narrower that contains an absent column, and mark `kept` when a gained column is absent. The one caller (`sql-driver-schema-sync.ts`) passes the result straight to `diffManagedIndexes`, which honours `kept`. The move is one direction only: orphan `drop_index` to nothing.
- **Resolved hash-shadow carrier: right.** On the widening arm a unique, non-partial carrier whose `shadowKey` resolves to exactly the narrower columns, any null-safe part being the tenant column's, is added to `explained` before the `present.length === 0` exit, so it is kept at every `kept`/certified/guard combination and never reaches `replace_unique_index`. Probe: `[]`, as the pins say.
- **Unresolved hash-shadow carrier: wrong, and stated as right** (must-fix 1). The claim loop skips `!p.shadowKey`; section 3 (the orphan arm) has no carrier exemption — only section 2 has `isHashShadowCarrier(p) && !p.shadowKey`, and that is reached by declared names only. Probe on this head, grant table, declared four-column global key, physical = an unresolved carrier under `uniq_sys_user_permission_set_ac248331` + the wide index: `[["drop_index","destructive","uniq_sys_user_permission_set_ac248331"]]`, the same with and without the guard, certified and not; with the gained column absent, the same drop beside a `create_index`. Controls in the same run reproduced the PR's own pins (resolved carrier `[]`; plain narrower + guard one safe replace).
- **P1 alone on main: harmless.** The grant key is still `unique: 'organization'`, which `widenedUniqueReplacements` does not take, so the grant table's plan is unchanged. For the other first-party unnamed global keys (18 declared on main by my grep, the activation ledger among them) every new answer replaces an orphan `drop_index` with nothing, or with a safe replace behind certification and a standing guard. No answer is added that drops a key. Must-fix 1 is not a regression of main either: on main the unresolved carrier's name is declared, so section 2 skips it. It becomes the destructive orphan when P2 respells the key, which is exactly the outcome must-fix 3 of 6774837781 was raised against.

### ② Semver level

- `patch` on `@objectstack/driver-sql`, no `!`, no BREAKING banner: correct for the level. `Metadata-protocol: none` is correct (a driver plan, no authorable key). Both lines are line-initial in the PR body and the changeset. The ADR-0087 marker is present though not owed on a non-breaking changeset; harmless.
- **`Clause-②: no` with no arm: accepted.** Nothing a caller could write or was served is refused; the three moves are a destructive plan offer becoming a kept index or a gated safe replace, each written FROM → TO. `(narrowing)` would wrongly make it BREAKING. Note for the seat: the committed lines therefore decide no narrowing face by themselves; this record is served at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` on the seat's claim (6779612699) because P1 carries must-fix 3 of a narrowing-face FAIL.
- FROM → TO completeness: the three declared lines match the code. The fourth case — an unresolved carrier — is declared under "Unchanged … still left alone", which is false after P2 (must-fix 1).
- First-party count: none is stated. Not owed for a non-narrowing, but the changeset's "any other declared global key … only in the three shapes" would be stronger with the count and the evidence named (nit).

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Author:** the PR's `user.login` is `os-support-ai`, not `objectstack-fleet[bot]` (written off-relay). Read before landing.
- **Must-fix 3 of 6774837781: closed for a resolved carrier, open for an unresolved one.** Kept and nothing offered: done for the resolved key, plain or NULL-safe, certified or not, guard or none. Pinned at the differ: four KEPT cases, the not-yet-physical case, two CONTROLs. Declared: the third FROM → TO line. 维护者速读: corrected — it now says the shadow case is kept and that only pure-function pins exist. The gap is the carrier whose generation expression could not be read (`resolveHashShadowKeys` swallows a failed `information_schema` read and skips an expression `parseHashShadowKeyParts` cannot parse — and no MySQL or MariaDB spelling of the grant key's shadow has been read live).
- **A kept shadow carrier has no way out, and the plan is silent.** The uncertified COALESCE case is released by the ownership ceremony; a shadow-carried narrower is kept "certified or not and with or without the guard", so after P2 a MySQL/MariaDB store whose grant key is shadow-carried keeps the three-column key for good and cannot hold two packages' same-named sets, with no plan entry saying so. That is the seat's ruled disposition and is accepted here. P2 must declare the consequence where it widens the key (should-fix 2).
- **The certified safe replace rests wholly on ADR-0131 D1.** On a table certified by marker whose tenant column is still physically nullable, the replace swaps a key that folds NULL-organization rows for a wider key and a guard that are both NULL-distinct on the organization. The diff's pins measure the non-NULL organization only and say so. Accepted on D1's premise; epic condition 1's NULL-organization pin for this table belongs to P1b's guard and is owed there.
- **Live dialects.** No MySQL or MariaDB has run this arm; the job that would is skipped on PR and merge-group events, so it first runs on `main`. Declared in the changeset and the PR body. The dogfood figures (26 tests) are the author's local run on base f71bb4135, 32 commits before this head's base; the Dogfood shards did not run on this head.

### ④ Design judgment

**must-fix**
1. **An unresolved shadow carrier under the narrower's name is still offered as a destructive orphan `drop_index`, and the diff says it is left alone.** Three texts state it: the code comment at the claim loop ("an unresolved carrier stays not-ours-to-reconcile, as the orphan arm already treats it" — the orphan arm does not), the changeset's "Unchanged" paragraph and the PR body's "one whose key could not be read is still left alone". The ruling (6774853256) is "a shadow-carried narrower is kept and nothing is offered", with no carve-out, and the module's own rule since cd1348802 is that a carrier is never proposed for destruction on a guess. Fix in P1: on the widening arm, account for a unique carrier under a `legacyNames` entry whose `shadowKey` is absent (add it to `explained`, offer nothing); pin it at the differ beside the four KEPT cases, with and without the guard; add it to the declared-ablation set; correct the three texts. The existing CONTROL (a carrier that resolves to other columns stays the orphan arm's) is right and stays.

**should-fix**
2. Record for P2, in its changeset: on a store whose grant key is shadow-carried, the three-column key stays and the widened key's capability is not delivered there, with the manual remedy or a filed card.
3. The ablation is described in the PR body only (shadow-carrier claim removed: 5 red, 10 green). There is no declared ablation for the NULL-safe `present` branch or for the absent-gained-column `kept` term; the test title "before this arm: a destructive drop_index" asserts their red state without a recorded run. Record both.

**nit**
- State the first-party count: which first-party global keys reach the arm on main, and that the 18.0 dogfood plan is unchanged for them.
- `isNullSafeTenantNarrower`'s `p.columns.includes(tenantField)` is implied by `nullSafeColumns` being a subset of `columns`; harmless.

**Tried and held:** resolved carrier, plain and NULL-safe, certified and not, with and without the guard (kept, `[]`); plain narrower with the guard (one safe replace, unchanged); a carrier resolving to other columns (orphan, unchanged); the tenant arms (the NULL-safe admission is gated on `widenedBy`, so they are untouched); every listed column absent (arm skipped); a narrower containing an absent column (never enumerated); a partial carrier (not claimed, still runtime-managed); the grant key on main (`'organization'`, not taken).

Reviewed-by: `session_01WGufzeeBmtefMTT21doena`
